description: MULTIPLY THE SPECTRUM BY A SAVED UNITARY MATRIX: every analysis window's channel vector is matrix-multiplied by a random unitary matrix read from a text datafile, scattering each frequency's energy across ALL channels - a total spectral scramble that preserves the sound's time envelope. CDP argv 'matrix matrix 2 infile outfile inmatrixfile [-c]': the matrix file rides the post-output aux slot; analchans/winoverlap are NOT parameters here - both are read from the file (source-pinned format, unitary_matrix.c:46: first value = analysis-overlap 1-4, then N*N complex entries as real/imag line pairs, N = FFT channel count; a 4-channel matrix is 9 lines, a 1024-channel one 524289). The ONLY practical producer is sibling mode 1 via execute() (e.g. execute(['matrix','matrix','1','in.wav','mymatrix','1024','3']) writes mymatrix.wav + mymatrix.txt - mode 1 itself is uncuratable: dual output, and its matrix is clock-seeded via initrand48()=srand(time(0)), differing run to run, same-second collisions byte-identical). Hand-written matrices are guarded: 'ERROR: WARNING: Matrix data does not have zeros on the diagonal. Not a unitary matrix.' (INVALID DATA). Given a fixed matrix the render is DETERMINISTIC (byte-identical 1.3 s apart) and the same matrix can be reapplied to any mono source (self-described dimensions - a 4-channel matrix verified on multiple inputs). -c applies the matrix CYCLICALLY (window n gets matrix^n; render verified distinct). Duration static, sample-exact. MONO ONLY ('ERROR: File st2.wav is not MONO'). Re-applying mode 1's saved matrix does NOT byte-reproduce mode 1's own sound output (verified - treat mode 2 as its own instrument).
musical_use: The deep end of the matrix family: where modes 3-4 apply one fixed algebraic twist, this applies a saved random rotation of the whole spectrum - pitched material becomes dense inharmonic spray, noise becomes strangely resonant, yet the phrasing and dynamics of the source remain legible. The matrix file is a reusable IDENTITY: generate one with mode 1 (execute), then stamp the SAME scramble onto a whole family of sounds for a consistent 'other world' - the reuse is the point, since mode 1 alone can never repeat itself. Small matrices (analchans 4-64 at generation) behave like wild fixed EQ-ring-mod hybrids; large ones (1024+) dissolve pitch entirely. -c makes the scramble PROGRESSIVE (matrix, matrix squared, cubed... per window) - the sound corkscrews further from itself as it plays. WATCH LEVELS: energy concentration is matrix-dependent and can be violent - a 0.5-peak tone hit +16.6 pre-clip with one 1024-channel matrix (CDP clips and prints 'You should reduce source level to avoid clipping: use gain of <= 0.060261') while a 4-channel matrix peaked at 0.754. Attenuate the source first (modify loudness) and check the render.

inmatrixfile.description: REQUIRED unitary-matrix text datafile, occupying the argv slot AFTER the output. Format (source-pinned): line 1 = analysis window overlap (1-4; out-of-range refuses 'Invalid analysis overlap val ... (range 1 - 4)'), then N*N complex matrix entries as alternating real/imag lines (N = FFT channel count; dimensions are inferred from the file). Produce it with mode 1 via execute() - the '<stem>.txt' half of its dual output; any extension except .brk works. Hand-made files must satisfy the zero-diagonal unitary check (refusal verbatim in the entry description).

cyclic.description: Apply the matrix-transform cyclically: window 1 gets spec*matrix, window 2 spec*matrix^2, window 3 spec*matrix^3... (banner + source matrix_cycle). Render verified distinct from the plain application - the scramble deepens over time.

examples.description: Stamp one saved scramble onto a sound.
examples.expected_use: mymatrix.txt from a prior execute(['matrix','matrix','1','seed.wav','mymatrix','1024','3']) run. Same matrix on other mono sources = one consistent alien timbre family.

examples.description: Progressive corkscrew away from the source.
examples.expected_use: Each window multiplies in another power of the matrix; the sound starts near the plain scramble and drifts further as it plays.

known_issues: LEVEL LANDMINE: output level is matrix-dependent and can explode - +16.6 pre-clip observed from a 0.5-peak source with a 1024-channel matrix; CDP hard-clips at full scale and prints the exact corrective gain ('use gain of <= 0.060261'). Attenuate the source first and inspect the render's peak.

The only practical matrix producer is mode 1 via execute() (dual-output + clock-seeded initrand48, unseedable, same-second collision trap) - save the .txt and reuse it; you can never regenerate the same matrix.
Applying mode 1's saved matrix does NOT byte-reproduce mode 1's own sound output (verified, shas differ) - the two modes are separate instruments sharing a matrix.
Hand-authored matrices are guarded by the zero-diagonal/unitary check and the overlap range check (both refusals verbatim above); dimensions must be a complete N*N complex table or parsing fails.
MONO ONLY ('ERROR: File st2.wav is not MONO'); duration static sample-exact; deterministic for a fixed matrix (verified 1.3 s apart).
No numeric parameters at all: analchans/winoverlap live inside the matrix file; nothing is breakpoint-capable.
version_sensitive: standnew program (dev/standnew/unitary_matrix.c, no HTML manual); matrix file format and all quoted refusals pinned from source + this build.
